metadata.description: Materials Project entries removed from every fetched or cached convex hull. 'elements': elemental entries keyed by element and matched by material_id or by (element, spacegroup_number); 'category' is 'spurious' (no stability field at 1 atm at any temperature: high-pressure, thin-film, purely computational, or ranked by GGA below the 1 atm ground state; the default when absent) or 'sgte_corrected' (a real 1 atm phase whose enthalpy the unary database takes from SGTE or another assessment, kept off hulls so its DFT energy is never used). 'status' marks records derived from GGA energies whose literature review is pending. 'ss_structure' (BCC, FCC or HCP) marks a computational prototype entry below the ground state whose solid-solution reference the unary database takes from omegas or SGTE. 'compounds': rules for non-elemental artifacts, each with one 'match' predicate: 'material_id', 'composition' (exact atom counts in the cell) or 'element_count' (counts of the named elements only). 'expected_gs_spacegroup': each element's 1-atm ground-state space group, with its basis in 'expected_gs_basis'; an elemental entry below it with another space group is also removed.
metadata.policy: Literature-verified 'spurious' entries have no reported ambient-pressure stability field (NIST TN 2312, D.R. Burgess Jr., 'Phase Transition Temperatures of the Solid Elements at Atmospheric Pressure', 2025). Real low-temperature allotropes are listed only as 'sgte_corrected'.

Ag.source: NIST TN 2312 (2025), Z=47; Fan et al., Nat. Commun. 6, 7684 (2015)

Hg.reason: High-pressure gamma-Hg, stable only between 12 and 37 GPa.

Equilibrium phase at 1 atm only below 79 K, where it lies 122 J/mol below alpha-Hg (dS = -1.54 J/(mol K)), but it does not form on cooling: it needs ~0.4-1 GPa or cold work below ~80 K and reverts to alpha-Hg above ~90 K. Kept off hulls because alpha-Hg is the reference above 79 K and GGA misplaces beta-Hg (-1666 J/mol vs alpha, c/a 0.87, against the measured -122 J/mol and c/a 0.707). Body-centred tetragonal, not bcc. TN 2312 lists alpha-Hg as the only solid at 1 atm.
Hg.source: Atoji, Schirber & Swenson, J. Chem. Phys. 31, 1628 (1959); Swenson, Phys. Rev. 111, 82 (1958); Guminski, J. Phase Equilib. 13, 657 (1992); Schulte & Holzapfel, Phys. Rev. B 48, 14009 (1993); Young, Phase Diagrams of the Elements (1991)
